utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Prlic et al. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Registrar. This is Tuesday, and I greet our witness, the accused, the Defence counsel, the representative of the OTP, and everyone helping us. I believe that our Registrar has an IC number for us. He has the floor.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The Prosecution has submitted their objections to documents tendered by 3D for admission through Witness Bozo Pavlovic. This list shall be given Exhibit IC01126. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mrs. Alaburic, you have the floor to continue with your examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Good morning to you to, my colleagues from the OTP and the other Defence counsel. Good morning to the accused, to the witness and everybody who is with us at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: We analysed yesterday the order by Enes Kovacevic, which was document 2D246. It's dated 14 April 1993. Witness, let us now try to see what subsequently happened in the Konjic area. Please look at document P1874. This is a summary report for the 13th of April, and let us see what it says about Konjic. The first report says that the village of Buscak was attacked and that the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina tried to cross the lake from Ostrozac and take Mount Falanovo, but they were stopped there. And it goes on to say that Butorovic Polje was shelled and that Kostajnica was being shelled, and that combat activity is starting at Konjic, which is blocked just as Jablanica is. Is this description accurate in accordance with your information, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let us look at the second report from Konjic on that day. The village of Buscak -- or, rather, the fall of the village of Buscak is imminent. It is requested that our earlier request is -- is granted. What kind of request was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is about the shelling of the Muslim positions from which the Croatian villages were being attacked.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let us look at the following paragraph. It says stronger enforcements arrived from Jablanica, then moving toward Mrakovo and Zuglici, and want to take Boksevica. Tell us, Witness, if we remember the documents that we saw earlier about the plans of the ABiH, does this direction correspond to the documents that we saw about the plans of the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's in line with those plans. One unit from the 1st Battalion which was tasked to take this area toward Zuglici and Mrakovo.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let us look at report number 3 from the same document with the same date. It says: “There are strong attacks from mortars against Ljesovina, Buturovic Polje and Kostajnica, and I skip one part. An ultimatum was issued to Radesine. Forces from Bosnia threatening Konjic, movements of the ABiH from Tarcin have been noticed and then comes a statement: "This is an all-out attack on the entire zone of Konjic and Jablanica." Is this an accurate report, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is very accurate.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let us look at the following document, P1879. It's an exhibit already, so we won't dwell on it long. Just to get the entire picture let us look at item 4. It reads: "Fighting has started in Konjic as well. The Croatian villages of Obri and Vrci have been attacked. We have no reports from Buscak, and there are attacks against Bucurovici [phoen] and Falanovo Brdo." Was it really that way, Witness, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was really that way.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let us look at the part of the report that refers to Prozor. It's the fifth paragraph in this part of the report. It says that the Herceg Stjepan Brigade asked for support from the Rama Brigade. It's the artillery support that we mentioned, isn't it, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: It goes on to say: We have forbidden the opening of artillery fire before an order is received. Tell me, Witness, did you immediately get artillery support or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we didn't get it immediately.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at the final part. It says: The intelligence situation is unclear in the area of Konjic and Jablanica. Reports are not coming in from the commanders in charge. There's arbitrariness in the opening of fire. We don't [as interpreted] the strength of units and individual zones, et cetera. Can you comment this -- these statements from the report for us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: This report clearly depicts the situation in the brigade. We were taken aback with the attack and the scale of the attack. Some of our units had lost contact with the staff and with the commander so that individual commanders, even platoon commanders, asked various units around us for help. So it wasn't -- it was actually people panicking and asking for help.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Toward the end of the report from Prozor, and a report from Konjic was added to the summary report about the situation on the 15th of April at 3.00 a.m. It says: During the night massive movements of Muslim units were noticed. Their sabotage groups moving from Rodici and the municipality of Jablanica toward the strategically important mount of Boksevica. And now listen: Whoever holds that mountain, that is Boksevica, controls almost the entire Neretvica Valley. Tell me, Witness, is that really so, that whoever holds Boksevica controls the area in the Neretvica Valley?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. Not only the Neretvica Valley but also part of the Neretva Valley and the Jablanica lake from the entry into Jablanica toward Celebici in the direction of Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now let's go a few lines further down. The report says that what it boils down to is that the ABiH is trying to take Boksevica. In accordance with your information, was that really the case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the case.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's skip one paragraph and look at the statement saying that the artillery of the ABiH is firing from the Risovac Plateau. Tell us, was that really the case, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, this Risovac Plateau, is it anywhere near Sovicka Vrata and the villages of Sovici and Doljani?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And in the last paragraph about Konjic says that: We are asking from Prozor that they support us with artillery, and it says, if this is not done, that is, if there is no support, then we stand slim chances to get out of it. Was that really the case, that unless help arrives from outside that this position could not be defended?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If the ABiH had taken Boksevica, our 1st Battalion would have been in the same position as the 2nd Battalion, that is, completely surrounded.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Witness, look at the following documents now, please -- following document now, please, P1887?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Excuse me, Ms. Alaburic. Witness, on the top of the last page of this document I read: "That is why we are kindly asking you that the artillery, et cetera, fire." Now, this is signed by the chief of HVO General Staff who actually is the highest commanding officer, in fact. I am very puzzled about this wording. It is not -- a military commander normally does not kindly ask for fire but orders. Do you have an explanation for this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't see the translation at all. I'm not receiving translation. From the very start.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Does it work now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I'm receiving translation now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Good. The paragraph is on page 5 in the original, and it is the two, three, four -- fourth paragraph, I think, which starts with the words "Zato vas molimo," and the translation is: "We -- that is why we are kindly asking you that the artillery fire." I abbreviate here. And I am struck by this wording, because the document is signed by the highest commander, Brigadier Petkovic, and it is not the tone that one normally finds in -- in military language. The commander would order fire but not kindly ask, and I was wondering whether you could give an explanation for that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I haven't completely understood the question. Could you please repeat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I am wondering about the language used by the Commander-in-Chief, who kindly asks, that's the translation, for artillery fire; whereas in my own military experience, which I think I share with -- with everyone who knows about this matter, is that a commander orders fire. And the question is: Can you explain this surprising formulation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which paragraph is that? I haven't found it. When I read it, I hope to be able to answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I am still --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I have -- my microphone is burning. I'm still on the document P1879, and I go to the last page. I'm looking at the B/C/S version now, and there the third or fourth paragraph starts with the words "Zato vas molimo i trazimo" and so on. Have you found that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I have. Your Honour, this is a summary report signed by Mr. Milivoj Petkovic, and these are the words of the people who requested help. In this case our 1st Battalion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: So although it -- yes. Mr. Petkovic is not speaking himself but quoting what he heard from Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you. That's helpful to know. Excuse me for the interruption, Ms. Alaburic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, did you know that at the Main Staff every day there was a compilation made of all the situation reports come being from the field. For example, the Tomislavgrad report, the Vitez report, report from Bosanska Posavina, and report from Konjic, and the compilation of all these reports was then signed by the chief of the Main Staff, General Petkovic. Was that the way things worked? Every day all situation reports coming from the ground were compiled, which is why we have this report where there's a request for artillery. It's not General Petkovic that is asking an authorisation from himself. Of course not. Did you know that this was the mode of operation, or are you discovering it today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I haven't discovered it today. This is how things worked. There were daily reports from the smaller units to the Main Staff, and it was usual to send one report a day, and in case of need there would be several.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: We're now about to show how these reports are made. Please take a look at the following document: P1887. P1887. It's a report from your brigade, Witness, signed by the commander Zdravko Sagolj, and it's the final report from Konjic. This report says: We are requesting that the artillery fire from the Risovac Plateau and so on. Witness, is this report part of the summary report we saw a minute ago?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: If we have now clarified, we can move on to the following document, 4D83. A report from of the Lisin Battalion commander who was in the village of Bradina. It is dated the 15th of April, 1993. This is in the Konjic region, Witness, is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is in the direction of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the contents. On the 14th of April, the BiH Army took control of the facilities Buscak and HVO barracks. It goes on to say that they're proceeding to liberate Klis, and at the end of the document it is said, and I quote: "I believe that tomorrow is the decisive day and in the morning the action will start to liberate the town which is under heavy artillery fire from the aforementioned elevations. This time there will be no stopping. We will proceed until final victory, because we are now convinced that the HVO is the enemy of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina." Witness, with regard to the features that the BiH Army was attacking, is this part of the report correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell me, the way the developments evolved, would you say that the attacks intensified?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: At the end of the document it says: We propose that you should order that there will be attacks on Boksevica and Pisvir with a view to their liberation. As far as you know, was that the goal of the BH Army attacks at the moment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the following document which is 4D874. This is an order issued by the chief of the Main Staff, sent to the OZ Central Bosnia to the commander Tihomir Blaskic. It says that with regard to the newly arisen situation in the territory of Konjic, the HVO from Central Bosnia should undertake certain activities, certain combat activities, in order to link up the BiH Army forces or engage the BH Army forces and thus facilitate the situation of the HVO in Konjic. Witness, did you request for assistance from Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did. We did request assistance from Central Bosnia, because we thought that in case the HVO forces started moving towards Bradina, we would be able to stop the attack that was launched in the direction of Konjic and further afield.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I have a few questions on distances. This document 4D874 is a document that I must assess, and when assessing this document I must make sure not to make any mistakes. The Appeals Chamber on paragraph 332 of its Blaskic judgement noted that the Blaskic Trial Chamber had made a mistake when it had assessed Exhibit D269. And I don't want to make mistakes, so I'm going to ask a few questions to you. Could you tell me what the distance was between Central Bosnia and yourself where you were placed? How many kilometres were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The distance from Bradina to the part where we requested help in Kresevo Kiseljak and the OZ where Tihomir Blaskic was, the distance was about 20 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Twenty kilometres. Very well. And could you tell me, if you know, what is the distance between Bradina and Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Between Bradina and Ahmici? I can't answer that because I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, give us an order of magnitude. Is it more than a hundred kilometres, less than a hundred kilometres, 50 kilometres? A ballpark figure, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I was never in Ahmici. I wouldn't be able to tell you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You cannot help us. Fine. In this document -- this is a document where people are asking help from Tihomir Blaskic. Twenty kilometres away you can have logistical support. You might even have fire artillery support. Could you tell us whether that's possible?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We requested full military support in infantry and all the other accompanying things that go with infantry. We wanted a unit from the part of Kiseljak and Kresevo start marching towards Bradina and Repovci in order to stop the Lisin Brigade which was marching and advancing in the direction of Duboki Potok. And thus from Bradina, Zulfikar's men were advancing toward Podorasac, Ganjin [phoen], Galjevo, and towards Konjic as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. This document is dated April 15, 1993. This is an important date for the OTP, because in its pre-trial brief it says that the HVO made an ultimatum which was to expire on April 15th, and in his submissions the Prosecutor explains that Ahmici was attacked on April 16. Now, you were a soldier. You were on the field. Had you heard about this ultimatum sent to the BH Army and expiring on April 15, 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I never heard of such a document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're saying no, but remember that you are under oath.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Alaburic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Witness, did you personally speak to somebody from the Central Bosnia OZ?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Who?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were connected with a commander who did not introduce himself to me, and I spoke to the commander who said that he was the commander of the special MUP unit, and we asked them if they could take the axis that I've already mentioned in order to drew the attention of the forces that were advancing towards Konjic. However, the answer that we received from them was negative. They told us that they already had problems in their own territory where they were deployed.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Did any assistance from Central Bosnia ever reach you or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the following document, 4D453. It's already in evidence. Let's just look at it briefly. It is stated in here that forces that arrived from Bradina and Igman have attacked Konjic, that there's pressure from Jablanica in the territory of Klis, and then that Zlatar and Boksevica are encircled. It says: Hurry, inform Prozor. They say they cannot help us. They say they do not have orders. Further on it says: Boksevica, Konjic, Celebici and Radesine are burning. Please help. Further on it says: Include Kiseljak in the Mount Ivan sector. In Prozor tie up the forces with artillery until something more concrete is done. And the final sentence reads: Move while we're still alive. Can you please comment, Witness? Was this situation as drastic as is portrayed in the last sentence, by the cry that you can read here?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The situation was exactly as it is portrayed and described, but the words cannot describe how bad the situation was. Zeljko -- Zdravko Sagolj's cry does not begin to describe it when he says, Move while we're still alive. The situation was really that bad.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Look at the following document which is P1882. This is a report from your brigade. It says: Frequent armed provocations against our positions are taking place in Sovici. Muslim forces are carrying out movements and manoeuvres in order to encircle our forces in Sovici and Doljani. It is then stated: Muslim forces are moving from their position towards Boksevica across the lake. And then it says BiH Army are attacking Boksevica and the Neretvica Valley. This is what is happening according to the commander. Witness, what I just quoted, according to what you know, was that a true reflection of the situation on the ground or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is a true reflection of the situation on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I apologise. My client is telling me that there are problems with the headphones and the interpretation. I can't talk to him. Could somebody from the technical service do that? I don't know whether that is the same case with the other accused. Maybe somebody could check whether all the ear -- headphones are plugged in properly and switched on to the right channel.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: We can then continue. Witness, let's look at the following document which is 3D557.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, let me return to this document about Sovici and Doljani, which is at the very heart of this topic. I understood that you confirmed how the situation was. As far as you know, the Sovici and Doljani, were they encircled by the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Those places were not encircled at the time. If you remember the document that we showed and that was an order from the commander from Jablanica, he did send some of the forces towards Sovici and Doljani and they were waiting for further attack orders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as you know, were there troop movements, ABiH troop movements in Doljani and Sovici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, around that time, on the 14th, 15th and 16th, all the units were mobile, which means that there was an all-out action that had been ordered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You say all the units, but you mean ABiH units and HVO units? Which were the mobile units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] BiH Army units. They were carrying out the plan that we saw yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What you're saying is important. The OTP may not be on the same wavelength, but you are under oath and you say that on the 14th, 15th, and 16th of April, the ABiH units were moving, among other places, in Sovici and Doljani. To your knowledge, in those locations were they HVO units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I know, there were HVO units in Doljani and Sovici. And for the unit that was tasked with preventing assistance to the HVO from Posusje, that unit had to block the unit that was supposed to receive the other units, which is only logical. And according to our information, those units from Jablanica were supposed to disable the units that were waiting to be received.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Vesna. I'm sorry, Your Honours. Mr. Stojic still cannot follow the proceedings. He still has go on switching between one channel to the next, and Mr. Pusic has the same problem. Maybe we could have somebody into the courtroom from the technical service because the usher himself was not able to deal with the problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Witness, your last sentence is not clear. You said the units that were coming from Jablanica were supposed to disable the units that were waiting to be received. We don't understand from this sentence who was arriving, who was receiving whom, who was encircling whom. If you are talking about units, could you please be more specific and tell us whether you're talking about the BiH Army or the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: The BiH Army units were tasked with disabling the units of the HVO which were deployed in Sovici and Doljani villages.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And the HVO units in Sovici and Doljani, if I can decipher your sentence properly, were supposed to receive assistance that was supposed to come from the direction of Posusje.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may have misspoken. In case those units of the HVO in Sovici and Doljani, on the occasion of the arrival of assistance to cross from Posusje, it would have been easier for the units to be linked up with the local units instead of acting on their own in a headless way.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And can you tell us whether the BiH Army was active in any area to prevent the arrival of the assistance of the HVO from Posusje and linking up with the units of the HVO in Sovici and Doljani?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we saw that from the order issued by the Neza [phoen] Brigade, the commander from Jablanica. He issued concrete tasks for carrying out task, and there was even a sabotage unit that was tasked with infiltrating Risovac Plateau in order to destroy all the artillery weapons that belonged to the HVO. That was their task and you could see that from the document that we saw earlier.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, Witness, about Risovac and Sovicka Vrata. Are these two localities near each other?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let us look at the following document, 3D557. Let us now see the assessment of Arif Pasalic. On the 16th of April, 1993, he says that the HVO forces in the area of Neretvica -- that is west from Boksevica, around Klis; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: So Arif Pasalic says that the HVO forces are in a difficult position due to lack of manpower. Was it really that way, that they didn't have enough men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's exactly how it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: He goes on to say that the HVO forces demand that their artillery on Risovac fire at our positions north of Neretvica. Tell us, were there really such demands from your brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our brigade demanded that the forces at Risovac fire not at HVO forces but at ABiH forces that were in that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I apologise if I phrased it that way. Of course I didn't mean that the HVO should have fired at its own units. Let's go on to see what it says under item 3. The HVO units expect help and manpower from Prozor from the northern side and that the HVO troops at Kiseljak were ordered to help those units at Bradina. Was that really so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Help was requested. Arif Pasalic obviously had information about it, it must be from intelligence sources, that we asked for help from the directions of Prozor, Bradina, and Kiseljak, and he informs his people on the ground about the condition we are -- we were in.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Now Arif Pasalic, he orders his units to continue combat activities and not allow the arrival of new forces from the direction of Prozor via the villages of Kacuni and Grevici, as well as from the direction of Bradina. Tell us were they successful in blocking the arrival of help?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were successful and we didn't receive any help.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Arif Pasalic continues to order his units to synchronise and integrate the joint combat activities for successful combat performances and crushing the HVO forces. You were on the grounds -- on the ground at the time. In accordance with your information, did the forces of the ABiH act in this way, in a synchronised and integrated fashion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did. They had agreed to -- to that effect, and they signed a document with eight stamps that they would really act in the way that Arif Pasalic had ordered them to act.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let us look at document 4D85. It's a combat report by Esad Ramic. Did you know Esad Ramic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I knew him.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: It's a report from the command of the Igman operations group of the ABiH, dated 16 April 1993. Among others, it is stated that the Zlatar facility is encircled and operations continue. Tell us, Witness, is that an accurate statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the statement is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: It goes on to say the HVO forces are requesting assistance and regard to this feature their strength is ebbing. Tell us, Witness, is this a correct statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Toward the end of the report we can read the Babin Nos facility is blocked, and the operation to capture it will be launched only after Zlatar and Repovica. Tell us, Witness, where you were on the 16th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 16th of April, 1993, I was right above Babin Nos. It's the village of Zabrdje.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, Witness, is the statement that the area of Babin Nos was blocked on that day correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The final paragraph reads: It is interesting that the Konjic HVO is pleading for help which has been promised from Kresevo and Kiseljak. Ambushes have been laid on these routes. Let us repeat, Witness, and tell us once again, did you receive help and were their efforts successful?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: We never received any help from this direction.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let us look at the following document on which we will dwell somewhat longer. It's document 4D599. It's again a report by Esad Ramic. This one is dated 17 April 1993, at 2000 hours. Let us go through the parts of that report. It says that the Stari Grad facility's encircled. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: It goes on to say that the Zlatar facility is completely encircled by 60 soldiers of the Black Swans Unit. The Black Swans. Then what probably means 40 members of the special units of MUP Hadzici and 80 soldiers of the 7th Konjic Brigade. While tightening the encirclement of the facility, 20 HVO soldiers were captured. Tell us, Witness, are these statements correct, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: With regard to the Babin Nos facility, tell us -- I believe that the facility is on the list. Were you there on that day too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: It says that the facility is encircled and that all important facilities in town are under the control of the ABiH. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's all correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: It goes on to -- to provide information about the village of Radesine. I will quote what Esad Ramic, from the 4th Corps of the ABiH, is saying. I quote: "We will try to finish our work at Konjic as soon as possible and then launch a counter-attack with all our brigades in two directions. First, the direction Konjic-Jablanica-Mostar, and secondly, Konjic-Prozor-Rama." Please comment this part of the report for us, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: This part of the report submitted by Esad Ramic means that after the completion of the operations from Bradina toward Konjic and further on to Boksevica, where they wanted to link up with units from Jablanica, they would continue to carry out the action in the Neretva Valley, in the direction of valley, and further on to Capljina, Stolac, and as far as Neum. And the other direction, the one from Jablanica to the right, that is, in the direction of Prozor by taking the villages of Doljani and Sovici and reaching the Risovac Plateau, and on to Prozor, that is, Rama.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Take a look at the final part of this report where Esad Ramic says: We will finalise the liberation of Bosnia-Herzegovina toward the east and west. Please do not stop us and do not send us any negotiators. Tell us, Witness, can you comment this position of the 4th Corps of the ABiH for us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. If we remember the 23rd of March of the same year, when there was an attempt to carry out this action, that is, on the 23rd of March, and it was stopped by negotiations and by bad weather, that is, heavy snowfall, now Esad Ramic saw his opportunity. If there are no negotiations which could stop the action, he thinks that they have the ability to complete it.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let us skip the following document and look at 2D89.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When reading this document one is under the impression that there is indeed an ABiH offensive because everything is detailed. Stari Grad, Zlatar, Spiljani, Polje Bijela, et cetera, but at the last but one paragraph there is the following mentioned. The author of this document assumes that there is co-operation between the HVO and the Serbs. He even says that there is an artillery operation on Muslim villages from Borak. I suppose that Borak is under Serb control. If it isn't, please tell me if I'm wrong. And he also says that there is an open aggression of the Serbs and the Croats against the sovereignty of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. So the person writing this report emphasises a joint Serb and Croat operation. What do you say to this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was probably some shelling on the part of the Serbs those days, but if we look at where the fighting took place, if we go back, where the positions of Spiljani and Bijela are mentioned, these were on the confrontation line with the Serbs, and that is where the ABiH disarmed HVO members so that the Serbs also weren't sure what was going to happen, whether they would advance against them. So they probably shelled the villages mentioned here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So as I understand it, as far as you know, there was no joint operation of the Serbs and the Croats against the Muslim.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was no such military operation. We received some services from the Serbs, but we had to provide some services in return. There have been such instances. But these were merely commercial transactions in a manner of speaking, but we did -- we never engaged in any joint military operations.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us, Witness, this commerce or trade with the Serbs, when did it take place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, we were already in the enclave. It was after the 18th of April. The ABiH had already taken all surrounding villages in the Konjic municipality, and when only our enclave was left, then together with the soldiers and the civilians there were also about 150 Serbs, and in the day -- following days their number rose about 450. The Serbs were grateful for the service we provided to the -- to them then, and they returned -- returned a favour to us with some services that we needed later.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let us clarify. It doesn't seem clear enough. At the moment when the HVO units retreated to the enclave there were also some civilians coming with them; right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Were there some Serbs among those civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The figure you mentioned, 150 Serbs, is that the number of Serbs who arrived at the enclave with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It -- that's the number of people who arrived on the first day, and their total number amounted to about 450.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: What would have happened to you in that enclave if it -- that territory didn't lean on the Serb-controlled territory? Would you have been able to survive there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we wouldn't. We wouldn't have had a supply corridor to supply food or ammunition, or a corridor for saving the wounded, so that at that moment the Serbs were some sort of necessary evil, and with their help we took our wounded and our civilians to Stolac, to Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: All right, Witness. Let us go on to look at other documents. 2D89. It's a joint statement by Alija Izetbegovic and Mate Boban, dated April 18th, 1993. These two presidents agree to stop the conflict, to release prisoners. And tell us, on that day, the 18th of April, 1993, were there any conflicts in the area that you were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were still conflicts, because on the 18th of April they took the prominent elevations around Konjic, that is, Zlatar and Grad.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's look at P1959. That's the next document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, document 2D89 is an essential document because it is signed both by Izetbegovic and Mate Boban. Any reasonable Judge reading this document could infer two conclusions from it. Firstly, these two heads -- these two heads, Izetbegovic and Boban, are clearly telling their troops that confrontation needs to end immediately. The word "immediately" is actually stated. And that it is important to determine responsibilities at all unit level in order to find out what really happened. This is the first interpretation you could make of the document. Izetbegovic and Mate Boban seemed to have been bypassed by their troops on the field, who actually did pretty much anything. But the second interpretation is the following. These two personalities, in a very hypocritical fashion, agree on a so-called press release stating that there is a cease-fire. And as you just said earlier, it still went on after April 18th. Now, you were on the field, so could you tell us what is your own interpretation of this document signed by both Izetbegovic and Mate Boban?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can only say that this was a formality, that this was not implemented on the ground at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So you just said that this was very informally signed. This was not implemented on the ground. But do you have an explanation that would say why this was not actually implemented?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because of the entire operation that had been long in the making and in the preparation. Most probably one of the founders and advocates of that operation was Alija Izetbegovic. Therefore, the operation followed its course, the course that it should have followed, and of course that it was only logical that it would have been absurd for him to stop an operation, to stop that operation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I understand you correctly, there were two signatories, but the hypocrite was Izetbegovic, who had planned an all-out operation and who had no intention of stopping anything. That's your testimony, or did I understand you wrongly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you understood me quite well.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Witness, let's move on and let's see how many orders should have been issued for the BiH Army to stop the attacks much later. Let's look at P1959 [Realtime transcript read in error "P19959"]. This is an order issued by the chief of the HVO Main Staff based on the conclusions reached by Mate Boban and Alija Izetbegovic. The order was issued on the 18th of April, 1993, about the cease-fire. And, Witness, did you know about the existence of this order, and did you, on the ground, feel any changes with regard to combat operations on the part of the BiH Army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not see or feel any changes in the BiH Army comportment.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And did you for any moment until then engage in any attacks or engage in any kind of military actions that could be construed as attacks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We did not launch any attacks. We did not even have an occasion to launch an attack.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I repeat the document number because it was mis-recorded on line 13. The document number is P1959.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the following document, Witness. This is 4D445. This is a combat report by the BiH Army for the same day, and let's see what the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina was doing on that day. It says the BiH Army took Zlatar, the facility Zlatar, which was a very important communication hub in Konjic. Tell us, Witness, according to what you know, would this be correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is a correct claim.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: It also says here that the town was also concerned [indiscernible] under siege and two hours ago it was taken. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the claim is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And it says the BiH Army completely took the axis between Galjevo, Homolje, and Repovci, and that the village of Repovci was taken as well. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's a correct claim.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: It says as well that the villages of Ovcari and Vrbici [phoen] were also taken and that the corridor was broken between Bradina and Konjic. Are these claims correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, these statements are correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: It says that at this moment, the Neretvica Brigade is liberating the strongholds of the Croatian Defence Council Pokojiste and Cerici, and after they are taken, the entire right bank the Neretva will be free. Is that what really happened.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but the name of the village is Pokojiste and Cerici, yes. And the 7th Brigade thus linked up with the Neretva Brigade from Klis as a result of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: It says here the remaining strongholds on the left bank of the Neretva still need to be liberated, and their names are Turija, Zabrdje, Pomol, and Ljubina. The action has been prepared and will be carried out tomorrow. My question to you, sir, is this: One could conclude that the agreement on cease-fire has -- had come to nothing and that the BH Army was still planning actions for the following days. Tell me, were there offensives launched by the BH Army army on the following days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: It says further on: All operations of both of our brigades have vigorously started and are moving forward. Our goal is to liberate Jablanica as soon as possible and help it further. Witness, could you conclude from what was happening on the ground that this assessment is correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a correct assessment. They were so much stronger than us that they could have easily carried out their plan.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the following document which is 4D1156.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Alaburic, to make sure that you can organise yourself, because you still have a few documents to go through, let me tell you that you only have 20 minutes left. So try and use your documents wisely.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the following document which is 4D1156. This is a report from the Rama Brigade, and let's look at the last paragraph, Witness. It says: In Konjic Muslim extremists are trying to take certain facilities. In their units there are also women who are "working on prisoners" in inverted commas. They're treating them and hiding them. It is noticeable that units which are active in the sectors of Konjic and Jablanica are mostly composed of people from outside, who are not locals, and they particularly hail from Eastern Bosnia. Those are mostly those who were fleeing before Chetniks and decided to stay in these Croatian regions and found shelter in them. According to our information, they were being organised and incited against Croats by extremist Muslims who had first created chaos in Prozor and then fled to Jablanica." Witness, remind us, when we were talking about the secret mobilisation in the month of February 1993, a document that was signed by Alija Izetbegovic, that document and that mobilisation applied to refugees. Do you remember where those refugees were from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those refugees were from Eastern Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: You told us, Witness, if I understood you properly, that the units that comprised refugees as well were a bit more radical and extreme in comparison with units composed of local Muslims. Did I understand you properly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you did.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: When I compare that statement that you provided yesterday with the assessment of the Rama Brigade, would you say that this conclusion reached by the Rama Brigade is correct or incorrect?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a correct conclusion and it's a proper conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's now look at the following document which is 4D90. Again a report from -- a report from the 4th Corps for the 22nd April 1993. The BiH Army in its report says: In the course of the day, in Konjic, we carried out intense combat activities. We gave up on the liberation of the villages of Turija, Zabrdje, and Zaslivlje, until we liberate the village of Radesine. Witness, tell us, please, was that the situation on the ground that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the following document which is 4D139. 4D139. This is a report or information on Konjic, a list up and down villages. The signatory of this document is Zarko Keza. Actually his name is printed, but, Witness, do you recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise Dinko Zebic's signature. He was Zarko Keza's deputy at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Is this document based on information provided by you or information provided by the 1st Battalion of your brigade?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, let's redact lines 14 and 15 because that might help identify the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour. I was careless in this particular instance.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Witness, please tell us, is this report from the 1st or the 2nd Battalion of your brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first part is from our 1st Battalion, dealing with the villages, and the second part of the report hails from the 2nd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: According to what you know, the information contained in this document, is it correct or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the information contained in this report is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the following document which is 4D137. 4D137. This is a document issued by the Office for Refugees and Displaced Persons of the HZ HB, which lists information about killed civilians and members of the HVO in the village of Trusina. Witness, tell us, please, do you know anybody from the list?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I used to know Ivo Drlja [phoen] very well. I also knew Stipo Ljubic and Zeljko Blazevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: They were HVO soldiers judging by the list; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct. Stipo Ljubic was a member of the police administration prior to that, as well as Zeljko Blazevic who was a reserve policeman.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Witness, tell us, please, in Bosnia-Herzegovina over the past few weeks, were proceedings launched with regard to the crimes committed against Croats in Trusina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Some people were arrested.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the following document which is 4D91. Again issued by the BH Army on the 24th of April, 1993. The document says: Our forces, with the forces of the Hadzici, Konjic and Jablanica MUP, put up fierce resistance to the Chetniks and inflicted heavy losses on them. What I'm interested at the moment is the issue of -- the issue of Hadzici, Konjic and Jablanica municipalities. Are these the municipalities whose representatives of the army and the police met on the 20th of March, 1993, and reached the conclusions that we analysed at some length which are contained in document 4D454? I would like to correct the date. No, I'm not correcting the date. The date is okay.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Those are the very municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And it says here at the end: The plan is to continue along the entire front and to link up Vrci and Ravni, and to link up all the forces in Jablanica. Witness, at that moment what was happening with Konjic? Had Konjic been taken or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that moment, Konjic was already taken. The only things remaining were the small enclaves of Drecelj, Zabrdje, Zaslivlje, and Turija. And at that moment, Vrce, which is a small village in the area of responsibility of our battalion, that was still free.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I'm going to read to you several orders issued by the BH Army about cease-fire and then after that there will be a question. The first document is 4D96. Sefer Halilovic's order about the end of all offensives, issued on the 25th of April, 1993. I skip two documents, and I would like to show you 4D435. Arif Pasalic's order dated 26th April 1993, which orders immediately to cease all offensive actions again the HVO units. And the word "immediately" is in block print. I skip two documents. Let's look at 4D549 now. This is Sefer Halilovic's order dated 28 April, where it says: "I'm most sharply warning you to immediately conduct unconditional and absolute cease-fire against the HVO units." The following document is 4D548. It's an order issued by the deputy Chief of Staff --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: I said -- I said what I will do.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, yeah, because I'm expecting a question to the witness, but I hope that will come.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I said that I would list all cease-fire orders and then ask a question, because I think that it would be wasting the Court's time to ask the same question about each order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Continue. Go on.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: The next document is 4D548. It's an order issued by Jovan Divjak, the deputy chief of the Supreme Command headquarters, dated April 28, in which also he orders the immediate cessation of all combat activities. The next document is 4D551. Arif Pasalic's command: Cease all operational activities and fortify the achieved lines, the lines reached. The next order is 4D436. Arif Pasalic's order dated April 29: "I warn you most severely to implement immediately an unconditional complete cease-fire against the formations of the HVO." My question to you, Witness, is: Were these orders implemented on the ground at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were not followed. The ABiH continued its activities.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And now my final question, Witness. There are two maps at the end of this binder. The first one is 4D1216. 1216. It shows the situation in the area of Mostar, but we are interested in Konjic now, in June 1993. From this simplified representation of the situation on the ground, we can see that in the area of Konjic at that moment there were two Croatian enclaves. In the one below, you were. You were in the one below, Witness, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And the other enclave was held by the 1st Battalion of your brigade around Kostajnica. Is that a correct representation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Let us look at the following map now, 4D129 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Sorry, correction, 4D1219.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: It shows the situation from September 1993. Now there is only one enclave, namely the one where you were. Is that correct, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us the date and the month as of which only one small Croatian enclave was left in the Konjic-Jablanica area.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: The date is roughly in mid-July 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Tell us the share of the Muslim population at Konjic at that moment.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that moment the share was over 90 per cent of the overall population.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm looking at the second map. I believe General Petkovic drew this map himself. In green, we see zone controlled by the BH Army; in pink, the zone controlled by the Serbs; and in blue, HVO-controlled areas. And this is reflecting the situation as of September 15, 1993. When looking at the Mostar area on this map, I note that from Mostar there's possibility of going south, but the direction is blocked off by the HVO, but it's -- there is a possibility to go north, however, without running into any problems. You were in the small blue enclave at the top of the map, and could you tell us whether this map correctly reflects the military situation in September 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it does, except for this one part behind Turija should have been in contact with the VRS-held area. If I may show you. Here in this part the map should be corrected.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe the witness can correct it and then we can assign an IC number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please make the correction. You will be given a marker. Just a minute. Nothing's happening. Could you please repeat what you just did. It would be maybe best to work with the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It can be initialed, then, 4D-AP [as interpreted], and could I please ask for an IC number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could we please have a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The document just marked by the witness which is a replica of 4D01219 shall be given Exhibit IC01127. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mrs. Alaburic you've run out of time. If you have one last question, please put the question to the witness and then we'll have our break.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I merely have a correction.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Witness, when we spoke about the share of the Muslim population in Konjic there was a mistake in the transcript. Namely, some language from which we -- it could be concluded that we were referring to the then share of the Muslim population at Konjic, and I meant the present share, nowadays.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what I said was the current percentage of Muslims at Konjic. It is certainly over 90 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: And my last question: As far as you know, does -- do the Sarajevo authorities nowadays encourage the return of Serbs and Croats to Konjic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, thank you. I have finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We'll break for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Cross-examination is to start with the other parties. Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. We will not be cross-examining the gentleman, but we do wish to thank him for coming here to give his evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 2D. I have a document from Mr. Stojic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. The Stojic Defence will want to cross-examine the witness, but according to our internal agreement, Mr. Coric's Defence is first today, so we should actually proceed in that order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Mr. Coric's Defence has no questions to -- of this witness. We thank him for coming and giving evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So 4D has no questions. Then -- 5D had no questions. 6D?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Mr. Pusic's Defence has no questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 3D, for Mr. Praljak?

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Thank you. General Praljak's Defence will have one brief question for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So as I understand it, Mr. Stojic's Defence will start.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I will start the examination now.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Witness - this is what I will call you - I hope that you are about to receive the documents based on which I will examine you. I will follow the examination-in-chief. And let us go back to the very beginning, 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would all unnecessary microphones please be switched off, the microphones of the Judges notably.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Please take a look at document 2D765, the very first document in my binder. Witness -- I will repeat. It is 2D765. That is correct. Witness, yesterday you said, and it is noted on page 23, lines 2 through 5, that the HVO had good co-operation with the ABiH and almost a Joint Command up until May or June 1992. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This is a document signed by Mr. Rusmir Hadzihusejnovic, president of the Presidency, that is the War Presidency of the Konjic municipality. And in this order he says that the defence forces of Konjic municipality are tasked to make sure that there is joint consumption of crude oil for all members of the defence forces, and in brackets he mentions the TO and the HVO. Was it that way at the time? Were operations conducted jointly as we see that oil is also used jointly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is exactly the way it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you. I will now deal with the events of the 23rd of March, 1993, which you described in detail, and therefore please look at document 2D639.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the sake of the transcript, I would like to point out that Witness Dragan Juric, who gave evidence before this Trial Chamber on the 27th of April, 2009, in transcript number 39038, lines 3 through 8, described these events in an identical fashion, I mean the events of the 23rd of March of 1993, which you described also.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This is a report by Marko Stanic, commander of the 1st Battalion called Klis. He says that on March 23rd, there were major conflicts in the area around Klis. He also said that a mixed delegation arrived from Mostar and truce was agreed upon. There was also an exchange of prisoners. There are efforts to calm down the situation. Witness, was the situation really as described in this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is just the way it was on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I will ask you to repeat what you have already said in the examination-in-chief. Did the conflict stop on that day, and if so, why?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this day, when the joint commission arrived, the conflict stopped in our 1st Battalion, whereas in the 2nd Battalion there had been no casualties and no conflicts. There was only disarm -- there was only disarmament of Croats in a part of the town of Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the sake of the transcript, I would like to repeat something that we have already seen, that there was an order by Mr. Milivoj Petkovic and Mr. Arif Pasalic about the cessation of conflict. I'm referring to document 4D125.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I'd like to ask you this: When the joint commission came, were you there? Did you see them arrive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I wasn't present when they arrived. I wasn't there at the time. I have already said that I was at the Zlatar facility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But did you know that there was a joint commission that was about to come?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We knew about it when the commission arrived. We were informed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm trying to see the logics in this document. If there are incidents between the HVO and the ABiH at a local level, it would be logical if the higher echelon were to go on the ground in order to appease everybody. This could be one explanation provided by this document. But this would also mean, and this is where I seek your advice, this would mean that the higher echelon did not control the lower echelons, and therefore that there could be at any time an incident. What do you think of this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Incidents could happen, because units were on the ground, and units tasked to produce incidents tried to bring about such situations in various ways. And in this instance, there was the -- an order from a higher level to try and calm the situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So there were units that were tasked to produce incidents? In saying this, you blame the ABiH. You put the responsibility onto them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, yes. At the very beginning we said that there were units that came from somewhere else, and there was also a unit under strength of -- or, rather, under the command of a certain Muderiz.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So if we understand correctly, if there had been no unit coming from outside, such as this Muderiz unit, there would have been no incidents. But since there were people that came from the outside, they caused incidents and hence the intervention of the joint commission. Is this your explanation for these incidents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If only the locals had remained and if no units had come from elsewhere, there would have been very slight possibilities for any incidents to break out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Among the HVO troops were there Croats coming from elsewhere or were there only locals?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In my municipality, Konjic, there were only local -- locals. Nobody came from anywhere else.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Witness, let's go back and follow up on His Honour Antonetti's questions about the incident or the attack, if we look at the documents of the BH Army. Was this BiH Army attack which happened on the 23rd of March, was that the implementation of the agreement between the units of the BiH Army? Under 4D454, you analysed the minutes under that number in great detail yesterday with Mrs. Alaburic and you confirmed that the attack on the 23rd of March was the product of the agreement within the framework of the BiH Army to launch that operation. Am I right in thinking that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And you also said that that attack was stopped very early on because there was a lot of snow on that day.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said that the snow did fall. Maybe not on the 23rd, but in the next few days.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Just to be able to see what you said, I'm just going to say what the BiH Army did on that day in Konjic. And there's a document speaking to that. The number is 4D438. You don't have to look for it. I'm just doing this for the transcript. You won't need the document. I'll just remind you that this is report issued by Commander Cerovac on the 23rd of March, reporting on what had happened on the 23rd of March. There is another report by Mr. Kolakusic and --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment. Let me finish the sentence.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Under number P172 [as interpreted] that was shown to you and which speaks about the same incident.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Go ahead and I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have an objection to one of the questions that was raised by Ms. Nozica. She says to the witness, referring to his evidence from yesterday: "And you also said that the attack was stopped very early on because there was a lot of snow on that day." Now, I think what the witness said was that on the 24th, it started to snow, but I don't think that he said the attacks stopped because of the snow. I think that's an inference that's been made by Ms. Nozica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Nozica, please clarify the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. If there has been a misunderstanding, let's ask the witness to clarify.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that the operation was stopped because of the large quantity of snow which fell two days after the beginning of the conflict. So it wasn't on the 23rd but, rather, between the 24th and the 25th, and that's exactly what I said.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a technical problem. I have to keep on switching off my microphone. On page 41, line 14, I would like to correct the number. I mentioned document number P1712.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now, I'm now going to ask you to move on and see what happened on the 24th of March, 1993. Look at the document 2D641. This is a report issued by Mr. Zdravko Sagolj, the brigade Herceg Stjepan commander, dated 24 of March, and he says here that the situation in the territory of Konjic was getting increasingly complicated. He said that the BiH Army had killed three HVO members who were first taken prisoners. They're using civilians as human shield. They do not allow us to get to our wounded soldiers. All the Croatian villages are encircled owing to the supremacy in manpower. And he says: The cease-fire that was agreed yesterday evening was used by the BiH Army only to exchange their members from our prisons, and then they carried out a regrouping -- regrouping and launched fierce attacks on everything Croatian. Can you confirm, Witness, that that was indeed the following day, the situation in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Witness, I would now like to discuss some documents that are connected with your testimony in the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, please. Looking at this document, I see that there were three HVO members that had been captured, and they were killed by the ABiH. If this document is accurate, so three soldiers were killed by the ABiH. We can also read that civilians were used as human shields. I'd like to know the following: In Konjic and in the wider area, were there UN troops? Was UNPROFOR present?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Spanish Bat was in charge of that part of Konjic at the time. And they were UNPROFOR, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this kind of situation, when the commander of the Herceg Stjepan Brigade, Mr. Sagolj, noted that soldiers had been killed, to your knowledge, did he go to see the commander of SpaBat to tell him to do something, to intervene with the ABiH, or were -- was there notice of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know whether there was any meeting of the kind, but as far as I know, there were none.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As for you, did you have contacts with SpaBat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I personally did not have any contacts with them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, please. Can we move into private session, Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Witness, I would like to talk about the month of April. Earlier today we saw a series of documents speaking about the events in the month of April or, rather, the attacks of the BH Army against the HVO in the month of April. Could we now look at the document number 2D403, which supports everything that you said about the dates when things happened. We have a report here issued by Mr. Sagolj, the commander, in which Mr. Sagolj says that the BiH Army had stormed the brigade headquarters in Konjic, disarmed all those who were found there at that moment. He speaks about barricades in several places within the very centre of the town. He also says that the apartments of Croatian citizens being looted. He also says that people were being arrested, and he says that in Klis the fightings were -- was intensifying and going on during the night. Could you please confirm that the situation on the 15th of April in Konjic is reflected by this report?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can confirm that because our brigade was disarmed on that day, and some of the command staff that was found in the brigade on the day were brought in.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Witness, when it comes to members of the HVO and citizens, were they being arrested around that time, and if they were, where were they taken, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS 4D-AB [Resumed]
utterances.text: Around that time members of the Croatian people and the HVO were being arrested and taken to the sports hall in Konjic. Certain individuals were also taken to the premises of the social and political organisations that existed in Konjic. Those were usually or exclusively political officials who were members of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And now I would kindly ask you to look at the following document, which is 2D78 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One moment, please. This morning, Witness, I asked you a question, and I didn't know then that the Petkovic Defence would present this document to you. This morning I mentioned an ultimatum by the HVO, on the 15th of April, and I asked you whether you were aware of the ultimatum. You said no, you'd never heard of it. I was not aware of this document when I asked you the question, but here I see that on the 15th of April it is the ABiH that disarmed HVO soldiers. Based on this, I ask myself this: If there was an overall plan by the HVO with an ultimatum and action, how is it that in Konjic the HVO did not take any steps, and that, on the contrary, they were victims of the disarmament action whilst they were the ones that should have disarmed the others? How do you account for this? Is it so that in Konjic you were taken by -- or surprised to see that, on the 15th of April, the ABiH disarmed the soldiers? Was that total surprise for you or was that something that you could actually foresee?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I told you that there was no ultimatum on the part of the HVO as far as Konjic municipality's concerned at least. Starting with the first conflict, on the 23rd of March until the 14th of April, there were a lot of tensions. The situation was tense all the time. At that moment we didn't really expect anything to happen, because we thought that the period was rather calm. However, things were reactivated on the 14th of April.
